COVID-19 Academic Impact in Indiana

 Damian Betebenner & Adam Van Iwaarden
 Center for Assessment

 Indiana TAC Meeting
 January 27th, 2022

Update on Academic Impact Analysis and Report
• We last met in late October and discussed findings.
• The July Board of Education presentation indicated overall academic impact
 was moderate/large in ELA and large in mathematics.
• Both status-based analyses as well as growth-based analyses support these
 findings.
• Since then we have finalized results associated with:
 • ILEARN spring 2021 summative assessment
 • WIDA-ACCESS 2021 summative assessment
• Today we want to share results associated with the analyses as well as some
 supplementary results requested by the TAC during the previous meeting.

 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 2

How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• The pandemic was like a “headwind” that (presumably) slowed down the learning of
 students due to a variety of factors.
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
 • Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
 • ILEARN: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID growth.
 • ACCESS: Use historical consecutive-year growth norms and compare to pre-COVID growth
 • NWEA-MAP: Provides growth data based upon historical norms but we currently don’t have historical
 growth to compare to.
 • Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
 • ILEARN: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
 • ACCESS: Use 2020 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
 • Adjustments include (potentially) imputation for missing data as well as propensity score matching for
• NOTE: When providing 2021 data, users will (correctly) want to compare their data to
 2019 (or 2020 with ACCESS). The task is to make sure that such a comparison is an
 apples-to-apples comparison.
 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 3

How do we quantify academic impact using test data
• Historical consecutive and skip-year growth norms were created for ILEARN and ACCESS in
 May, 2021 for use with 2021 ILEARN and ACCESS data.
• We can use test data in two ways to quantify the impact of this headwind:
 • Best way: Quantify how much the rate of learning (i.e., growth) slowed:
 • ILEARN: Use historical skip-year growth norms to quantify growth and compare to pre-COVID growth.
 • ACCESS: Use historical consecutive-year growth norms and compare to pre-COVID growth
 • NWEA-MAP: Provides growth data based upon historical norms but we currently don’t have historical growth to
 compare to.
 • Next best way: Look at how much 2021 status changed:
 • ILEARN: Use 2019 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
 • ACCESS: Use 2020 status (or some adjustment thereof) as a proxy.
 • Adjustments include imputation for missing data as well as propensity score matching for changes in
 demographic characteristics of the population.

• Indiana participation rates were normal, with participation exceeding 95% in all grades
 and content areas.

Qualifying Academic Impact
To help summarize the vast quantity of results for stakeholders, we created
categories of academic impact based upon both effect size standards.

 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 6

Review of results: ILEARN
• Academic impacts in mathematics were larger than those in ELA,
 though impacts were large in both content areas.
• Academic impacts were consistent in size across grades.
• Across demographic subgroups, academic impacts were fairly uniform.

 Pandemic Related Academic Impact in Indiana 7

Review of results: WIDA-ACCESS
• For English Language Learners taking the WIDA-ACCESS English
• Academic impacts were large for students in the elementary grades.
• Academic impacts were moderate for students in middle school
 grades.
• Academic impacts were modest to none for students in the high
 school grades.
